summary: I wrote plan.md for a logging camp on a 40 × 34 block clearing beside a rutted road. It has a dark spruce-log bunkhouse with notched corners, a front porch and a stone cook chimney, plus a tall open sawmill (end facing the road, vent on the ridge, brick boiler stack). Both roof specs passed a dry run with no warnings. It reads as a lumber camp because the logs go in from a log pile at the front, pale sawn boards come out to a yard at the back, and the clearing is full of stumps.
concept_subject: A northern lumber camp in a cut-over spruce clearing, seen from a rutted logging road of brown dirt and gravel. On the left stands a long, low log bunkhouse of dark bark-on spruce logs on a grey cobblestone plinth. At its corners the logs cross and stick out past the walls, alternating with each course. A steep grey slate-shingle gable roof runs along the road, with a dark eave and pale stripped-spruce boards filling the two gable triangles. A covered plank porch runs along the front under a low shed roof on pale posts, with a simple spruce rail and two hanging lanterns either side of a spruce door. Shuttered square windows sit in the log walls. A chunky mossy fieldstone chimney rises outside the east gable, past the ridge, puffing cook smoke. Cordwood is stacked under the west eave, and an open woodshed lean-to sits at the back. To the right, separated by a dirt path, stands the taller sawmill: an open pole frame of pale stripped-spruce posts with knee braces and a heavy top beam. Its 45° grey slate gable faces the road, with a plank gable end, a small loft door and a SAWMILL sign, and a louvred vent runs along the ridge. Inside, the dark interior shows a saw carriage running from front to back. In front of the mill, a log deck of bark-on logs piled in a low pyramid on skids is ready to roll in. Against the mill's east side, a red-brick boiler stack with a dark band and a stepped cap sends a tall white column of smoke high above the camp. Behind the mill, three stacks of pale fresh-sawn birch boards with dark spacer strips stand in the lumber yard along dirt lanes. Stumps are scattered across patchy grass, coarse dirt and podzol. A chopping block sits by the back path, and tall dark spruce cones close in at the edges of the lot.
concept_size: 40 wide, 34 deep; a 1½-storey log bunkhouse (walls 6 high, ridge at y=14) and a mill hall of the same height (ridge at y=14), with smoke stacks up to y=19
